question: How many paintings from the Rijksmuseum are in the collection?
sparql: SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?w) AS ?n) WHERE { ?w a mc:Work ; mc:museum "rijksmuseum" }
explanation: Counts the distinct paintings in the graph whose source museum is the Rijksmuseum. The graph only holds paintings made between 1850 and 1900, so this is not the Rijksmuseum's full collection.

question: How many paintings by Claude Monet are there?
sparql: SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?w) AS ?n) WHERE { ?w mc:artist ?p . ?p rdfs:label "Claude Monet" }
explanation: Counts the distinct paintings, across all three museums, that are plainly by Claude Monet. Works only attributed to him or made after him are left out.

question: Which Vincent van Gogh paintings does the Met have?
sparql: SELECT DISTINCT ?w ?title WHERE { ?w mc:artist ?p ; mc:museum "met" ; dcterms:title ?title . ?p rdfs:label "Vincent van Gogh" }
explanation: Lists paintings at the Met that are plainly by Vincent van Gogh. Works only attributed to him, made after him or by imitators are left out.

question: Which artists have paintings in all three museums?
sparql: SELECT ?p ?artist WHERE { ?w a mc:Work ; mc:artist ?p ; mc:museum ?museum . ?p rdfs:label ?artist } GROUP BY ?p ?artist HAVING (COUNT(DISTINCT ?museum) = 3) ORDER BY ?artist
explanation: This lists artists with at least one painting at each of the Rijksmuseum, the Met and the Art Institute of Chicago. It counts only works plainly by the artist, not ones merely 'after', 'attributed to' or 'workshop of' them.

question: How many artists have works in more than one museum?
sparql: SELECT (COUNT(?p) AS ?n) WHERE { { SELECT ?p WHERE { ?w a mc:Work ; mc:artist ?p ; mc:museum ?m . } GROUP BY ?p HAVING (COUNT(DISTINCT ?m) > 1) } }
explanation: Counts the artists whose paintings are held by at least two of the three museums. Only works plainly by the artist are counted, not ones merely 'after', 'attributed to' or 'workshop of' them.

question: Show me landscapes at the Rijksmuseum.
explanation: Finds Rijksmuseum paintings whose subject has a name containing "landscape" (for example "landscape" or "landscape painting"). It includes both subjects the museum recorded and subjects suggested by AI.

question: Which Impressionist paintings show snow?
explanation: Finds paintings whose museum-stated style or the artist's Wikidata movement is Impressionism and that have a snow subject. The snow subject can come from the museum's own record or from an AI suggestion.

question: How many paintings have subjects that were suggested by AI rather than recorded by the museum?
explanation: This counts paintings with at least one AI-suggested subject (confidence 0.6 or higher) that the museum did not also record for that painting. Paintings where the AI only repeated the museum's own subjects are left out.

question: Which paintings did the AI tag with night that the museum didn't?
explanation: Finds paintings where the AI suggested a subject labelled "night" (confidence of at least 0.6) but the museum's own recorded subjects include no concept labelled "night".

question: When was Berthe Morisot born and when did she die?
sparql: SELECT ?birthYear ?deathYear WHERE { ?p rdfs:label "Berthe Morisot" . OPTIONAL { ?p mc:birthYear ?birthYear } OPTIONAL { ?p mc:deathYear ?deathYear } }
explanation: Looks up the person labelled exactly "Berthe Morisot" and returns her birth and death years as recorded from Wikidata. The graph holds only years, not full dates.

question: Which artists in the collection belong to the Hague School?
explanation: This lists the artists whose Wikidata movement is the Hague School and who are plainly credited with at least one painting in the collection. Artists who are only linked through attributions such as "after" or "workshop of" are not included.

question: How many paintings were begun in the 1880s?
sparql: SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?w) AS ?n) WHERE { ?w a mc:Work ; mc:beginYear ?y . FILTER(?y >= 1880 && ?y <= 1889) }
explanation: Counts the distinct paintings whose recorded begin year falls between 1880 and 1889 inclusive.

question: How many paintings does each museum have?
sparql: SELECT ?museum (COUNT(DISTINCT ?w) AS ?n) WHERE { ?w a mc:Work ; mc:museum ?museum . } GROUP BY ?museum ORDER BY DESC(?n)
explanation: This counts the paintings (made 1850–1900) held in this graph for each museum: the Rijksmuseum, the Met and the Art Institute of Chicago. Results are sorted from the largest collection to the smallest.

question: Which five artists have the most paintings?
sparql: SELECT ?artist (COUNT(DISTINCT ?w) AS ?n) WHERE { ?w a mc:Work ; mc:artist ?p . ?p rdfs:label ?artist } GROUP BY ?p ?artist ORDER BY DESC(?n) LIMIT 5
explanation: Counts the paintings plainly credited to each artist across all three museums and lists the five with the most. Works only 'after', 'attributed to' or 'workshop of' an artist are not counted.

question: Find paintings of boats from before 1870.
explanation: Finds paintings begun before 1870 whose subjects include boats or ships (also matching labels like sailboat, vessel and watercraft). It includes both museum-recorded subjects and AI-suggested subjects.

question: How many artist records were matched by a person approving an AI suggestion?
sparql: SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?a) AS ?records) (COUNT(DISTINCT ?p) AS ?people) WHERE { ?p mc:sourceAgent ?a . ?a mc:matchMethod "human-approved" }
explanation: This counts museum artist records with the match method "human-approved", and how many distinct people they link to. The graph records only that a person approved these matches; it doesn't say whether an AI proposed them (its AI suggestions are about painting subjects, not artist matches).

question: How many paintings are not open access?
sparql: SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?w) AS ?n) WHERE { ?w a mc:Work . FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?w dcterms:license ?license } }
explanation: Counts the paintings that have no licence recorded, since the licence is missing whenever a museum's record is not open access.

question: Which paintings are only attributed to, after, or imitating Vincent van Gogh?
explanation: This finds paintings linked to Vincent van Gogh only through a qualified attribution, such as "attributed to", "after", "imitator of" or "workshop of". It matches any qualified person label that contains "van Gogh" and shows that label so you can see which kind of attribution applies.

question: Portraits of women at the Met
explanation: This finds Met paintings tagged with a portrait subject and also with a woman, women or girl subject. It includes AI-suggested subjects as well as the ones the museum recorded.

question: Which Impressionist painters have works in more than one museum?
sparql: SELECT ?artist (COUNT(DISTINCT ?museum) AS ?museums) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?museum; separator=", ") AS ?which) WHERE { ?p mc:movement ?m ; rdfs:label ?artist . ?m skos:prefLabel ?ml . FILTER(LCASE(STR(?ml)) = "impressionism") ?w mc:artist ?p ; mc:museum ?museum . } GROUP BY ?p ?artist HAVING (COUNT(DISTINCT ?museum) > 1) ORDER BY DESC(?museums) ?artist
explanation: This finds painters whose Wikidata movement is Impressionism and lists those with paintings in at least two of the three museums. It counts only works plainly by them, not ones marked 'after', 'attributed to' or 'workshop of'.
